feedback.overall:
1. Overall assessment  
Strong, credible CV for senior digital communications roles: the experience shows clear progression, relevant platforms, and solid scope across strategy, web, analytics, and multimedia. It reads polished and substantive, but it would be stronger with tighter structure, fewer repeated skill sections, and more quantified outcomes beyond activity descriptions.

1. Top strengths  
- Clear senior-level positioning with a coherent narrative from coordinator to director to consultant, which strengthens credibility.  
- Strong domain relevance: Drupal, analytics, governance, email, social, video, and advocacy/public-sector communications are all well aligned.  
- Writing is generally clear and professional, with no obvious misspellings or major grammar errors; tone is consistent and confident.

1. Top improvements  
- Reduce duplication: “Core Competencies,” “Topline Skills,” “Technical + IT,” and “Soft Skills” overlap heavily. Consolidating these would improve clarity and save space.  
- Add more measurable impact in several roles. Some bullets describe responsibilities well, but more outcomes (growth %, efficiency gains, engagement improvements, cost savings) would increase impact.  
- Fix minor style inconsistencies: use serial commas consistently (“web, content, email, social media, and multimedia” vs “web, email, social and multimedia”); standardize dash/bullet formatting; “12 years experience” should be “12 years’ experience” or “12+ years of experience.”
feedback.intro:
Quick assessment: Strong, credible intro that aligns well with the CV’s senior digital leadership focus. It would be sharper with one or two concrete differentiators and slightly less overlap with the competencies section.

Suggested rewrite improvements:
- Change “more than 12 years experience” to “12+ years of experience” for cleaner, standard phrasing.
- Add a clearer senior-value statement tied to recent work, e.g. enterprise web modernization, digital governance, and analytics-driven communications.
- Tighten the list of channels to avoid sounding generic; emphasize leadership of integrated digital ecosystems rather than naming every channel.
- Suggested rewrite: “Digital communications and strategy leader with 12+ years of experience leading integrated web, content, email, social, and multimedia programs for mission-driven organizations. Brings deep expertise in cross-channel communications, enterprise web modernization, digital governance, and workflow design. Strong track record in advocacy messaging, stakeholder coordination, and translating complex technical or policy issues into clear, accessible content.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Cross-channel communications” and workflow/system language overlap heavily with Core Competencies and Topline Skills.
- “Mission-driven organizations” is useful, but avoid repeating advocacy/public-sector phrasing elsewhere in the header.
feedback.coreCompetencies:
Quick assessment: Strong, relevant themes, but this block is broad and overlaps heavily with the header, Topline Skills, and Soft Skills. Tightening the phrasing and emphasizing higher-value leadership capabilities will make it more distinctive.

Suggested rewrite improvements:
- Replace generic terms with sharper, senior-level language: “Multi-channel communications leadership” instead of “Multi-channel communication,” and “Web platform governance” instead of “Web & CMS administration.”
- Group related items to reduce repetition and improve flow; suggested version: Digital strategy & transformation • Multi-channel communications leadership • Web platform governance & CMS modernization • Editorial workflow & content operations • Analytics, reporting & performance insights • Systems architecture & workflow automation • Stakeholder & cross-functional coordination • Advocacy, policy & public-sector communications • Multimedia, livestream & event production
- Use parallel noun phrases throughout for consistency.
- Consider prioritizing more recent strengths such as CMS modernization, analytics, and AI/search-related systems if space allows.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Stakeholder & cross-department coordination” duplicates Soft Skills and the header.
- Several items overlap with Topline Skills, especially digital strategy, editorial systems, analytics, and multimedia.

items.title: Strategic Communications Consultant
items.subtitle: Freelance (full-time engagement)
items.content:
Support a U.S.-based national membership organization on digital strategy, campaign platforms, content operations and enterprise web improvement.
- Build and refine digital systems, workflows and analytics that support coordinated organization-wide communications.
- Develop campaign and storytelling experiences within the organization’s Drupal platform, including custom microsite structures, modular content sections and downloadable member-facing toolkits.
- Deliver CMS development, front-end implementation and technical troubleshooting for large public-facing web properties.
- Advise on governance, usability and operational best practices across web, email, social and multimedia channels.
- Lead development of an AI-enabled search initiative, shaping retrieval strategy, structured content workflows and user-facing discovery design.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong, current role with clear strategic + technical scope, but it reads as a task list and overlaps heavily with the project footer and prior NACo entries. Tighten around outcomes, scale, and what is new at this level.

Suggested edit:
- Open with impact and client scope: “Advise a U.S. national membership organization on enterprise digital strategy, Drupal platform improvement, and cross-channel content operations.”
- Consolidate overlapping bullets into 3–4 sharper ones, e.g.:
- “Built and optimized digital workflows, analytics, and governance models to improve coordination across web, email, social, and multimedia teams.”
- “Designed and launched Drupal campaign experiences, including modular microsites, storytelling components, and downloadable member toolkits.”
- “Led AI-enabled search development, defining retrieval approach, structured content requirements, and user-facing discovery experience.”
- Add measurable outcomes where possible: number of sites/pages/users, publishing teams supported, reductions in turnaround time, engagement gains, or search/discovery improvements.
- Replace weaker phrasing like “support,” “advise,” and “deliver” with “led,” “built,” “designed,” or “implemented.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “AI-enabled search” and microsite details duplicate the Recent Projects section; keep this entry higher-level.
- Governance/analytics/workflow language overlaps with the Director of Digital Media role; emphasize consulting ownership and new initiatives.

items.title: Director of Digital Media
items.subtitle: National Association of Counties
items.content:
Led NACo’s digital communications team, overseeing the organization’s website, email, social media and video platforms, along with digital strategy, analytics, governance and budget management.
- Led the redesign and migration of NACo’s 10,000+ page website into a new Drupal platform supporting 3.5 million annual page views, 6,000+ average daily users and 50+ internal publishers.
- Directed NACo’s core digital communications channels, including email newsletters reaching tens of thousands of county officials and social media platforms serving thousands of followers.
- Built NACo’s first broadcast-quality in-house video studio, expanding in-house capacity for advocacy programming, event production and recurring multimedia content.
- Expanded the organization’s analytics infrastructure across GA4, Microsoft Clarity, Power BI, Looker Studio and BigQuery, improving reporting and strategic decision-making.
- Strengthened digital operations through clearer governance, publishing standards and cross-department planning systems.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong, high-impact leadership entry with good scale signals. It would be sharper if the opening were tighter and the bullets emphasized outcomes, team leadership, and transformation over channel oversight.

Suggested edit
- Replace the opening with a results-led summary: “Directed NACo’s digital media function across web, email, social, video, analytics, governance, and budget, leading platform modernization and cross-channel communications strategy.”
- Tighten and strengthen bullets with action + outcome: “Led redesign and migration of NACo’s 10,000+ page website to Drupal, supporting 3.5M annual page views, 6,000+ daily users, and 50+ internal publishers.”
- Add measurable impact where possible for email/social/video/analytics: audience growth, engagement rates, production volume, reporting speed, or cost savings from the in-house studio.
- Combine governance/analytics into one stronger operational bullet: “Built analytics and publishing governance across GA4, Clarity, Power BI, Looker Studio, and BigQuery, improving reporting, decision-making, and cross-department planning.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings
- “Directed core digital communications channels” overlaps with the prior NACo role; focus this entry on enterprise leadership and transformation.
- Video studio/buildout may partially overlap with earlier video-production bullets; frame it as scaling in-house capability, not producing content.

items.title: Associate Communications Director
items.subtitle: National Association of Counties
items.content:
Led day-to-day digital communications operations across web, email, social media and video, helping scale NACo’s editorial coordination and advocacy communications.
- Managed four recurring weekly newsletters reaching tens of thousands of county officials and public-sector stakeholders.
- Produced and expanded a weekly advocacy video update, helping establish video as a recurring policy communications channel.
- Strengthened editorial planning and coordination across communications, advocacy and program teams.
- Helped improve the consistency and effectiveness of NACo’s digital publishing workflows.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong progression story, but this entry overlaps heavily with the later Director role and earlier Digital Media Manager role. Make it more specific to what changed under your ownership at this level: editorial operations, newsletter scale, and launch/expansion of recurring advocacy video.

Suggested edit:
- Rewrite the lead to emphasize scope and function: “Managed NACo’s day-to-day digital communications operations across web, email, social and video, improving editorial coordination and advocacy publishing.”
- Tighten bullets around distinct outcomes: “Managed four weekly newsletters reaching tens of thousands of county officials and public-sector stakeholders.”
- Make the video bullet more active and outcome-led: “Launched and scaled a weekly advocacy video update, establishing video as a recurring policy communications channel.”
- Combine the last two bullets into one sharper line: “Built stronger cross-team editorial planning and more consistent digital publishing workflows across communications, advocacy and program teams.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Digital publishing workflows” and “editorial planning” are repeated in the Director role; keep this version operational/tactical, while the Director entry stays strategic/governance-focused.
- Weekly video updates also appear in the 2015–2018 role; frame this item as scaling/formalizing the series, not originating it.

items.title: Digital Strategy & Content Leadership
items.content:
- Enterprise digital strategy
- Editorial systems and governance
- Multi-channel communications leadership
- Public-sector and advocacy messaging
- Audience-focused content planning
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong positioning, but this skills block overlaps heavily with the header and Core Competencies. Tighten it to emphasize senior leadership scope and audience/governance strengths without repeating platform or channel language covered elsewhere.

Suggested edit:
- Replace with sharper, less repetitive phrasing:
- Enterprise digital strategy & transformation
- Editorial governance & content operations
- Cross-functional communications leadership
- Public-sector, membership & advocacy messaging
- Audience strategy, planning & content prioritization
- Use “transformation,” “operations,” and “cross-functional” to signal seniority and recent leadership impact.
- Swap “multi-channel communications leadership” for “cross-functional communications leadership” to avoid repeating channel-specific language already detailed in experience.
- If space allows, make one item outcome-oriented, e.g., “Governance models for high-volume publishing teams.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Enterprise digital strategy” and “Editorial systems and governance” duplicate both the header and Core Competencies almost verbatim.
- “Public-sector and advocacy messaging” overlaps with “Advocacy and public-sector communications”; vary wording or cut one.

items.title: Web Platforms & Technical Execution
items.content:
- Drupal
- WordPress
- SharePoint
- Power Pages
- CMS modernization
- HTML, CSS, JavaScript and jQuery
- API integrations
- Workflow automation
- Airtable systems
- AI-enabled search experiences
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong, relevant skill cluster, but it’s too tool-heavy and overlaps heavily with the “Technical + IT” section. In Topline Skills, this should emphasize higher-value platform leadership and execution themes rather than repeat a full software list.

Suggested edit:
- Reframe from tools to capability-led phrasing, e.g.: “Drupal and enterprise CMS delivery • CMS modernization and migration • Front-end implementation (HTML, CSS, JavaScript) • API integrations and workflow automation • Airtable-based operational systems • AI-enabled search and discovery experiences”
- Drop lower-priority or less evidenced items here, especially “jQuery,” unless it is central to current target roles.
- Put the strongest, most recent differentiators first: Drupal, CMS modernization, AI-enabled search, integrations/automation.
- If possible, align wording to proven outcomes from recent roles, e.g. “enterprise CMS modernization” or “large public-facing web platforms.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- This largely duplicates “Technical + IT”; avoid repeating WordPress, SharePoint, Power Pages, and Airtable in both places verbatim.
- “AI-enabled search experiences” also appears in Core Competencies; consider keeping it in only one section.

items.title: Analytics, Insights & Optimization
items.content:
- GA4
- Microsoft Clarity
- Looker Studio
- Power BI
- BigQuery
- KPI design
- Leadership reporting
- SEO and performance analysis
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong, relevant skill cluster, but it overlaps heavily with “Core Competencies” and “Technical + IT.” Tighten it to emphasize decision-making and optimization outcomes, not just tool names.

Suggested edit:
- Reframe as a value-led line, e.g.: “GA4, BigQuery, Looker Studio, Power BI and Microsoft Clarity • KPI framework design • executive reporting dashboards • SEO, UX and performance optimization”
- Replace “Leadership reporting” with “executive reporting dashboards” or “decision-ready reporting” for sharper phrasing.
- Consider swapping “SEO and performance analysis” to “SEO, UX and conversion/performance analysis” if accurate; it reads more outcome-oriented.
- Keep only the most differentiating tools/skills here; use this section to show strategic analytics capability, not a full software inventory.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- Nearly duplicates “Data, Analytics & Optimization” in Technical + IT; consider making Topline Skills more strategic and Technical + IT more tool-specific.
- “Analytics and reporting infrastructure” already appears in Core Competencies, so avoid repeating that exact framing.

items.title: Multimedia Production & Event Delivery

- Video production and editing

Quick assessment: Strong category, but it reads generic and overlaps with both Core Competencies and older NACo bullets. Make it more senior, tighter, and aligned to recent leadership-level multimedia work.

Suggested edit
- Rename to: Multimedia Production, Studio & Event Operations
- Replace with tighter, higher-level bullets:
- Broadcast-quality video production and editing
- Livestream and hybrid event production

- PTZ camera and multi-camera workflows

Duplicate/redundancy warnings
- “Multimedia production and livestream operations” already appears in Core Competencies; consider shortening one or removing that phrase there.
- “Studio operations” and “video production” are already evidenced in NACo roles, so avoid repeating lower-level phrasing like “virtual event production” unless it adds distinct value.

items.title: University of Virginia
items.subtitle: Bachelor of Arts (BA), Economics & History
items.content: Ranked among the top public universities in the United States
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: The current line adds little value and reads like generic school marketing. For an experienced candidate, this education entry should be minimal and factual unless you have honors or distinctions worth adding.

Suggested edit:
- Replace the content line entirely with no body text; the degree, school, location, and dates are sufficient.
- If applicable, swap in a concrete credential instead: “Relevant coursework: …” or “Honors: …” only if genuinely strong and still relevant.
- Tighten the subtitle to “B.A., Economics and History” for cleaner formatting.
- Consider dropping dates if you want to reduce age signaling and keep focus on recent senior experience.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Ranked among the top public universities…” is generic and not candidate-specific, so it weakens the entry rather than strengthening it.
- Avoid adding coursework unless it clearly supports current digital strategy/communications work; otherwise it will feel disconnected from the stronger recent experience.

items.title: Web Platforms & CMS
items.content: Drupal • WordPress • SharePoint • Power Pages • GitHub Pages
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid platform list, but it reads as a generic inventory and overlaps heavily with “Web Platforms & Technical Execution” in Topline Skills. Since Drupal is clearly the strongest/recent platform, lead with that and add light proficiency context.

Suggested edit:
- Rewrite as: Drupal (enterprise migration, microsites, modular content architecture) • WordPress • SharePoint • Power Pages • GitHub Pages
- If space allows, group by strength: Primary: Drupal • Working knowledge: WordPress, SharePoint, Power Pages, GitHub Pages
- Keep only platforms here; avoid broader terms like “CMS modernization” since that already appears elsewhere.
- If accurate, consider version/scope specificity for Drupal to reinforce recency, e.g., “Drupal 10.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- This item substantially duplicates the Topline Skills entry “Web Platforms & Technical Execution”; consider trimming one or making this version more platform-specific.
- GitHub Pages may feel lightweight versus the seniority of the rest of the CV unless it supports a notable project.

items.title: Coding & Technical Implementation
items.content: HTML5 • CSS3 • JavaScript • jQuery • API integrations • Google Tag Manager • Cloudflare Workers • GitHub Actions
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid technical coverage, but this reads as a generic keyword list and overlaps heavily with “Web Platforms & Technical Execution” in Topline Skills. Tighten it to emphasize implementation tools that support recent Drupal, analytics, automation, and AI/search work.

Suggested edit:
- Rename to: Front-End & Technical Implementation
- Replace with a tighter list: HTML/CSS/JavaScript (jQuery) • API integrations • Google Tag Manager • Cloudflare Workers • GitHub Actions
- Drop version numbers (“HTML5,” “CSS3”) unless required by the role; they add little value and date the section.
- If space allows, add one impact cue tied to recent work, e.g. “used for Drupal microsites, analytics instrumentation, workflow automation, and AI/search prototypes.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “HTML, CSS, JavaScript and jQuery” and “API integrations” already appear in Topline Skills; avoid repeating the exact phrasing in both places.
- Cloudflare Workers and GitHub Actions are the most distinctive items here—keep them prominent.

items.title: Automation & Workflow Systems
items.content: Airtable • Power Automate • Zapier • Jira • Asana • Basecamp • Slack • Teams • Trello
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Useful tool list, but it reads as a generic software inventory rather than evidence of workflow systems expertise. It also overlaps with “Workflow automation” and “Airtable systems” already called out in Topline Skills.

Suggested edit:
- Reframe from a pure list to a tighter, capability-led line: “Workflow automation & collaboration: Airtable, Power Automate, Zapier; project/work management: Jira, Asana, Trello, Basecamp; team collaboration: Slack, Teams.”
- Prioritize the strongest, most relevant tools first; if space is tight, cut weaker/redundant items like Basecamp or Trello.
- If accurate, add a light outcomes cue instead of only naming tools, e.g. “used to streamline editorial planning, approvals, and cross-team coordination.”
- Keep naming consistent with other sections and avoid overloading this item with general collaboration apps.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Airtable systems” and “Workflow automation” already appear in Topline Skills; consider removing one mention or making this item more tool-specific.
- Slack/Teams may feel low-value unless collaboration platforms are important to the target role.

items.title: Email & Engagement Systems
items.content: Dynamics 365 Customer Insights / Journeys • Higher Logic • Mailchimp
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: This item is relevant, especially given the recent emphasis on email leadership, but it reads as a basic tool list and misses the strategic/operational depth shown elsewhere. Tightening the label and adding context would make it feel more senior and aligned with recent roles.

Suggested edit:
- Rename to: Email Marketing, CRM & Community Platforms
- Replace with: Dynamics 365 Customer Insights / Journeys • Higher Logic • Mailchimp
- If space allows, add light functional framing: Campaign automation • newsletter distribution • audience segmentation
- Keep only platforms you’ve used meaningfully in recent roles; if one was limited or older, consider dropping it rather than listing three equally

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- This overlaps with repeated email/newsletter leadership already covered in NACo roles; avoid adding descriptive claims here that restate those bullets.
- “Engagement Systems” is vague and may duplicate “Automation & Workflow Systems”; use clearer platform-based wording instead.

items.title: Work Eligibility
items.content: Full legal authorization to work in Belgium (Visa D + residence permit / carte de séjour)
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Useful for Belgium-based applications, but the phrasing is a bit legalistic and takes more space than needed. This should read as a clear status note, not a headline achievement.

Suggested edit:
- Rewrite for brevity and recruiter scanability: “Authorized to work in Belgium (Visa D and residence permit).”
- If accurate, make it stronger and simpler: “Fully authorized to work in Belgium; residence permit in place.”
- Avoid the French term unless the role specifically requires bilingual administrative terminology; “residence permit” is usually enough.
- Consider moving this into the contact/header area for local applications, since eligibility matters more there than in a secondary rail.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- No major duplication, but this item is lower-value than recent experience; keep it very short so it doesn’t compete for attention.
- If location/contact already signals Belgium and applications are local, this may be optional rather than essential.

items.title: Languages
items.content:
**English** (Native)
**French** (A2/Learning)
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: This item is clear but too compressed and visually awkward. It should be reformatted for quick scanning and framed honestly so French supports your Belgium-based role without overstating proficiency.

Suggested edit
- Rewrite as a simple line: Languages: English (native) | French (A2, currently improving)
- Use lowercase proficiency style for consistency and cleaner tone: native, A2, conversational/basic if accurate.
- If relevant to target roles, add practical context only if true: French (A2, professional working improvement underway)
- Keep it concise; this section is supporting information, not a selling point versus your recent digital leadership experience.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings
- No major duplication, but avoid overdesign/bolding here; the CV already has strong skills sections competing for attention.
- If space is tight, this can stay in the rail and should not be repeated in the header, summary, or cover letter unless language is job-relevant.

items.title: Soft Skills
items.content: Cross-department coordination • Stakeholder communication • Team leadership • Strategic planning • Clear writing and editing • Problem-solving • Adaptability
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: This section is too generic and largely repeats strengths already proven in the summary and core competencies. On a senior CV, “soft skills” should either be removed or reframed as leadership traits tied to scope and outcomes.

Suggested edit:
- Rename to “Leadership Strengths” or “Management & Collaboration” to sound more senior and less filler.
- Cut generic items like “Problem-solving” and “Adaptability”; keep only traits that support target roles.
- Tighten to 4–5 items max, e.g.: Cross-functional leadership • Executive stakeholder management • Editorial judgment • Team development • Strategic planning
- If space is tight, remove this section entirely and use the room for quantified achievements in recent roles.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Cross-department coordination” and “Stakeholder communication” duplicate the header summary and Core Competencies.
- “Team leadership” and “Strategic planning” are already demonstrated more credibly in the 2022–2024 Director role.

items.title: References
items.content: References available upon request.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: This item adds little value and uses space that could better support recent, higher-impact experience. “References available upon request” is assumed by most employers and usually should be removed.

Suggested edit:
- Delete the “References” entry entirely.
- Use the freed space for stronger supporting content instead, such as a brief “Selected Results” rail item with 1–2 metrics from recent roles.
- If references are specifically requested, provide them separately rather than on the CV.
- If you want a replacement rail item, consider “Work Authorization” or “Languages,” which are more useful and already present here.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- This section is redundant because reference availability is standard and does not differentiate you.
- Keeping it may weaken the second-page rail by displacing more relevant, recent qualifications.

items.title: Digital Media Manager / Producer
items.subtitle: National Association of Counties
items.content: Advanced through two digital roles, supporting the creation of the organization’s first in-house digital team and strengthening workflows across web, email, social, and multimedia. Contributed to a major website refresh and produced high-impact digital content—including livestreams and weekly video updates—while providing day-to-day guidance to a digital media associate.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid progression story, but the item is too general and overlaps with the stronger NACo roles that follow. Make this entry more execution-focused and foundational, with concrete outputs rather than broad team/workflow language.

Suggested edit
- Rewrite to emphasize early-stage build work: “Promoted across two digital roles while helping establish NACo’s first in-house digital team and support day-to-day execution across web, email, social and video.”
- Add specific deliverables: mention the website refresh, livestream production, weekly video series, and any volume/frequency if known.
- Tighten phrasing and remove soft claims like “high-impact” unless you can quantify results.
- Possible rewrite: “Promoted across two digital roles and helped launch NACo’s first in-house digital team. Supported a major website refresh, produced recurring livestreams and weekly advocacy video updates, and contributed to daily publishing across web, email and social media. Provided day-to-day coordination and guidance for a digital media associate.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings
- “Strengthening workflows” overlaps with 2018–2022 and 2022–2024 entries; keep workflow language lighter here.
- “Weekly video updates” appears in the next role; frame this as helping launch/produce the series rather than expand it.

items.title: County Solutions & Innovations Coordinator
items.subtitle: National Association of Counties
items.content: Coordinated innovation and research projects supporting organizational programs and policy work. Contributed to digital content production and multimedia materials, and launched the organization’s first podcast, overseeing planning, scripting, and production.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid early-career entry that shows the start of your multimedia/digital trajectory, but it reads broadly and undersells impact. Since this is an older role, keep it concise and emphasize the podcast launch as the clearest differentiator.

Suggested edit
- Rewrite to foreground the most distinctive achievement: “Coordinated innovation and research initiatives supporting NACo programs and policy priorities.”
- Tighten the second sentence and make the podcast launch the headline outcome: “Produced digital and multimedia content, including launching NACo’s first podcast and leading planning, scripting, and production.”
- If you can, add scope or output metrics: number of episodes, audience, internal stakeholders supported, or types of research/projects delivered.
- Consider a sharper final version: “Coordinated innovation and research initiatives supporting NACo programs and policy priorities; produced digital and multimedia content and launched the organization’s first podcast, leading planning, scripting, and production.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings
- “Digital content production and multimedia materials” overlaps with later NACo roles; keep this entry higher-level and avoid repeating video/web workflow language.
- Don’t overemphasize team leadership here, since stronger leadership evidence appears in later, more senior roles.
